methodology.codeLineByLineReview: Read safeErrorMessage/safeErrorClass/classifyError line by line and mapped every property access/operator touching `err`: (1) `value instanceof Error` - independently try/catch-guarded in BOTH functions, never a bare `if`. (2) `.message` read - its own try/catch, entered only after the guarded instanceof passed. (3) non-string `.message` -> `String(msg)` - its own nested try/catch. (4) final `String(value)` fallback - its own try/catch. (5) `.constructor` read - its own try/catch inside the guarded instanceof branch. (6) `ctor.name` read - happens INSIDE THE SAME try block as `.constructor` (not a separate unguarded access), confirmed to cover two-level poisoning. No `in` operator, no `Object.prototype.toString.call`, no `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor`, and no `JSON.stringify` of the raw value anywhere in the guarded path (confirmed via grep) - so those specific hostile channels are structurally inert here rather than merely untested.

methodologyFinding.description: A genuine finding surfaced during this audit, but it is a TEST-FRAMEWORK artifact, not a production defect: globally poisoning `Error[Symbol.hasInstance]` (required to properly test that specific JS interception channel, since Symbol.hasInstance is looked up on the constructor operand of `instanceof`, not the value) breaks every `x instanceof Error` check in the whole process for as long as it stays poisoned - including inside vitest/chai's OWN `.toThrow()` matcher, which performs its own internal `instanceof Error` check even when the wrapped callback completes normally without throwing. An initial version of this test used `expect(() => safeErrorMessage(value)).not.toThrow()` while the global was still poisoned, and vitest reported a failure carrying the injected message - APPEARING to show classifyError leaking an exception. Direct reproduction with a raw try/catch (bypassing the assertion library entirely) and console-log instrumentation of an inlined copy of the guard logic proved the production function's own try/catch genuinely caught the poisoned instanceof and returned normally in every case; the second throw vitest reported originated from its own matcher's internal instanceof check, executed AFTER the production function had already returned. The final test file (committed) never invokes any assertion-library matcher while the global remains poisoned - it captures results via plain try/catch first, restores the global in `finally`, and only then asserts. This is disclosed here in full rather than silently worked around, since it could otherwise be mistaken for evidence against the fix.
methodologyFinding.reproducible: Poison Error[Symbol.hasInstance] globally, then call expect(() => anything).not.toThrow() inside vitest for ANY function, even one with no relation to error classification - the matcher itself fails.

dispositionRationale: Across 19 fresh, independently-invented hostile values (17 unit-level plus 2 additional through the full runContractAnalysis path, for 3 total end-to-end re-proofs) specifically targeting JS semantics distinct from the implementer's own matrix - Symbol.hasInstance interception on the Error constructor, has-trap-only Proxies, toStringTag divergence, getOwnPropertyDescriptor-trap Proxies, two-level constructor.name poisoning, thenables, callable Proxies, multi-hop circular+toJSON structures, absurd-size strings, frozen Proxies, isolated getPrototypeOf-only Proxies, revoked Proxy.revocable(), non-string .message with hostile coercion, boxed-primitive poisoning, selective per-property Proxy traps, and a Symbol.toPrimitive spec violation - classifyError, safeErrorMessage, and safeErrorClass never threw and always returned a well-formed {message: string, errorClass: string} pair. The implementer's own self-reported bug class (unguarded instanceof via a Proxy's getPrototypeOf trap) was re-attempted with a genuinely different combination (getPrototypeOf-only, and a revoked Proxy) and the fix generalized correctly rather than being a narrow patch. No falsifying case was found; the one anomaly encountered (Error[Symbol.hasInstance] global poisoning appearing to break the code under vitest's own .toThrow() matcher) was traced conclusively to the test framework's own internal instanceof check, not to the production code, and is fully disclosed in methodologyFinding above rather than omitted.
